concepts.def: A reaction that transfers heat to the surroundings, so the temperature rises; the enthalpy change ΔH is negative.
A reaction that takes in heat from the surroundings, so the temperature falls; the enthalpy change ΔH is positive.
Particles only react when they collide with at least the activation energy; more frequent or more energetic collisions increase the rate.
Breaking a solid into smaller pieces exposes more surface, so collisions happen more often and the reaction speeds up.
A substance that speeds up a reaction without being used up, by providing an alternative route with lower activation energy.
A reaction that can proceed in both directions; in a closed system it reaches a dynamic equilibrium.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Physical Chemistry — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Physical Chemistry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Physical Chemistry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The temperature of a reaction mixture rises as the reaction proceeds. The reaction is:
options: Exothermic
Endothermic
At equilibrium
Catalytic

mcqs.q: Which of these does NOT increase the rate of a reaction?
options: Decreasing the temperature
Increasing the concentration
Adding a suitable catalyst
Grinding the solid reactant into powder

mcqs.q: A catalyst speeds up a reaction by:
options: Providing an alternative pathway with lower activation energy
Heating the reaction mixture
Increasing the concentration of reactants
Being used up to release energy

mcqs.q: In a reversible reaction at dynamic equilibrium:
options: The forward and backward rates are equal
Both reactions have stopped
Reactant and product concentrations must be equal
Only the forward reaction continues

mcqs.q: Is a catalyst used up during the reaction it speeds up?
options: A higher concentration lowers the activation energy of the reaction.
Catalysts are consumed like reactants, so more must keep being added.
Catalysts gradually turn into the product during the reaction.
No — it is chemically unchanged at the end and can be reused; it works by providing a lower-energy pathway.

mcqs.q: Does increasing concentration make the particles move faster?
options: No — it packs more particles into the same volume so collisions are more frequent; only temperature changes particle speed and energy.
A higher concentration lowers the activation energy of the reaction.
A higher concentration speeds the reaction because the particles move faster.
Both bond breaking and bond making release energy.

mcqs.q: Is energy released when the bonds in a fuel break?
options: Both bond breaking and bond making release energy.
Catalysts gradually turn into the product during the reaction.
Burning releases the energy stored inside the fuel's bonds as they break.
No — breaking bonds absorbs energy; the heat from burning comes from the stronger new bonds formed in the products releasing more energy than bond breaking absorbs.
